description.value: Tse'k'wa National Historic Site is a Dane-zaa gathering place near Charlie Lake with over 12,500 years of living history, designated a National Historic Site by Parks Canada in 2019 and collaboratively owned by Doig River, Prophet River, and West Moberly First Nations. The heart of the site is a cave perched on a cliff above the Peace Valley, accessible via a 230 m interpretive trail through a landscape that includes a traditional healing garden and land-based cultural experiences. The site won the 2026 BC Tourism Industry Conference Indigenous Operator or Experience Award, recognizing its authenticity and contribution to Dane-zaa cultural resilience.

address.value: 12629 Butte Ln, Charlie Lake, BC V0C 1H0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website at tsekwa.ca provided rich content. The /visit/ page confirmed washrooms ('two universally accessible outhouses'), the address (12629 Butte Ln, Charlie Lake, B.C. V0C 1H0), and phone (250-224-7906). No bike parking, water refill, or other cyclist-specific amenities are mentioned anywhere on the site; absence of evidence leaves those null. The site is confirmed open for self-guided tours year-round.
concerns: OSM record has no osm_id, no address, and no phone — all contact details sourced from website only, so contact_confirmed fields for phone and address cannot be cross-checked against OSM.

OSM coordinates (56.2738°N, 120.9436°W) differ slightly from the website's listed coordinates (56°16′22″N, 120°56′39″W ≈ 56.2728°N, 120.9442°W) — minor discrepancy, likely the same location but worth verifying.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, open, publicly accessible National Historic Site with a functioning website and confirmed location; free admission makes it a natural stop for touring cyclists in the Peace Region.
enrichment_extras.notes: Admission is free; donations welcomed. The site explicitly cannot accommodate large RVs and notes that parking is limited — relevant context for touring cyclists arriving with trailers or cargo bikes.
